question:
In a trigonometric identity investigation, two acute principal angles are defined by $\alpha=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{7}{25}\right)$ and $\beta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{15}{17}\right)$. From the corresponding right-triangle ratios, $\cos\alpha=\dfrac{24}{25}$ and $\cos\beta=\dfrac{8}{17}$. The students analyse $\alpha+\beta$ using the sine and cosine addition formulas. Both the value and sign of $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$ must be checked before the sum can be represented using a single inverse-sine principal value. The principal-value range of $\sin^{-1}x$ is $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

(a) Calculate $\sin(\alpha+\beta)$.

(b) Calculate $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$.

(c) Determine whether $\alpha+\beta$ lies in the principal-value range of inverse sine.

(d) Express $\alpha+\beta$ as a single inverse-sine principal value.
explanation:
(a)
Using the sine-addition formula,
$$\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta+\cos\alpha\sin\beta$$
$$=\frac{7}{25}\cdot\frac{8}{17}+\frac{24}{25}\cdot\frac{15}{17}$$
$$=\frac{56+360}{425}=\frac{416}{425}$$

(b)
Using the cosine-addition formula,
$$\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta-\sin\alpha\sin\beta$$
$$=\frac{24}{25}\cdot\frac{8}{17}-\frac{7}{25}\cdot\frac{15}{17}$$
$$=\frac{192-105}{425}=\frac{87}{425}$$

(c)
Both $\sin(\alpha+\beta)$ and $\cos(\alpha+\beta)$ are positive. Hence, $\alpha+\beta$ is an acute angle satisfying
$$0<\alpha+\beta<\frac{\pi}{2}$$
Therefore, it lies in the principal-value range of $\sin^{-1}$.

(d)
Since
$$\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\frac{416}{425}$$
and $\alpha+\beta$ belongs to the principal range of inverse sine,
$$\alpha+\beta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{416}{425}\right)$$
Thus,
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{7}{25}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{17}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{416}{425}\right)$$

options.A:
(a) $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{304}{425}$

(b) $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{297}{425}$

(c) $\alpha+\beta$ is acute and lies in the principal-value range

(d) $\alpha+\beta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{304}{425}\right)$
options.B:
(a) $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{416}{425}$

(b) $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{87}{425}$

(c) $\alpha+\beta$ is acute and lies in the principal-value range

(d) $\alpha+\beta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{416}{425}\right)$
options.C:
(a) $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{416}{425}$

(b) $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=-\dfrac{87}{425}$

(c) $\alpha+\beta$ lies in the second quadrant and outside the principal-value range

(d) $\alpha+\beta=\pi-\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{416}{425}\right)$
options.D:
(a) $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{87}{425}$

(b) $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{416}{425}$

(c) $\alpha+\beta$ is acute and lies in the principal-value range

(d) $\alpha+\beta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{87}{425}\right)$
